___ is an ___ yo woman with a complex past medical 
history of atrial fibrillation, MGUS and prior strokes and DVTs 
who presents now with acute onset right sided weakness.

Exam 
was notable for right hemiplegia, right visual field cut, 
decreased sensation right arm as well as severe dysarthria.

CT 
demonstrated a
subacute left PCA infarct; CTA with left PCA irregularity, 
possible P1 occlusion.
Unable to obtain MRI due to pacer.

There 
is moderate athrosclerotic disease of the cerebral vessels, but 
suspect the cause of stroke to be either cardioembolic secondary 
to untreated atrial fibrillation or hypercoaguability, as the 
patient has had multiple blood clots in the last few years 
including PE.

She has a history of MGUS which may produce a 
hyperviscosity syndrome (Serum viscosity elevated: 2.3).

No changes were done with her antiplatelet agents (aspirin) 
given past GI bleed.

Echo unremarkable for cardiac source of embolus other than 
atrial fibrillation.

She is not a candidate for warfarin due to a prior 
episode of life-threatening bleeding while she was taking 
warfarin.
Warfarin also caused increased bruising in the past.

On admission some of her BP meds were held and she will likely 
need to restart some of these in the coming weeks.
